paragraphs: "Can you make it face you?"
Cole’s eyes flicked toward the gap, then back to Dexter. "For how long?"
"Two breaths."
Cole smiled thinly. "You got it!"
He stepped into the center lane, plasma flaring around his arm. The attack struck the wyvern across its snout, and its head jerked toward him.
"Bulwark!"
The tank drove into the creature’s leg. Gridlock raised a barrier behind its other foot, obstructing the movement as it tried to turn.
Bullet Spear Man struck the wing joint, and Blitz flashed past its eyes.
"Rooooooar!!!"
The wyvern roared and Dexter moved as lightning flickered around his boots as he crossed the broken street, stepped onto a fallen block of stone, and launched himself beneath the raised wing.
His saber entered the exposed gap, and he twisted and drove through. A brilliant line appeared across the creature’s body.
The wyvern froze, then burst into thousands of fragments. Light scattered over the entire street as the remaining smaller creatures dissolved.
"Ding!"
[SIMULATION COMPLETE]
[All Hostile Targets Eliminated]
[Extraction Route Secured]
[Three Injured-Party Markers Preserved]
For a moment, nobody spoke. Then Blitz fell backward onto a low wall. "I have decided," he announced, "that I dislike flying reptiles."
Bulwark looked at him. "You said that after the second wave."
"My position has strengthened."
Cole laughed, and Dexter lowered his saber and looked around at the others.
They were breathing hard, sweating, more tired than any of them would have admitted when they entered.
But the difference between their first attempt and the last was impossible to miss. They had begun by competing with one another’s instincts. By the end, those instincts had started working together.
Dexter glanced at the place where the wyvern had disappeared. No system notification followed.
Of course not—light and formation energy did not count as a living enemy. The two kills he needed would have to wait.

They remained in the arena long enough to review their performance. Cole replayed the final exchange, Gridlock identified a point where he had wasted mana protecting empty space, Dexter acknowledged that he had moved too early during one of the flank changes, and Bullet Spear Man admitted, with visible reluctance, that his first attack on the larger wyvern’s wing had been poorly angled.
Blitz claimed his only mistake had been arriving without a meal, and that complaint eventually became persuasive.
By the time they returned the training equipment, everyone was hungry.
"There’s a restaurant near the rest courtyard," Cole said. "Still inside the facility. The food is decent."
Dexter checked the time. He had enough room for a meal before heading home, so he sent a short message to his wives: ’Training is finished. Eating with the team, then coming home.’
Lyra replied almost immediately. ’Is the food better than yours?’
Dexter smiled. ’Ihaven’t tasted it yet.’
’I don’t think it would be’
He shook his head and put the phone away.
The restaurant stood beside a broad courtyard within the Titan complex.
Glass doors faced an open seating area beneath a row of shade trees, and heroes occupied most of the tables, some still wearing training equipment.

The Facility staff moved between buildings with tablets and supply carts, and a group of younger trainees sat near the fountain, arguing over the results of their own session. Everything looked ordinary and busy.

They chose a long table near the windows. Bulwark sat first, and the chair creaked. He looked down at it with faint suspicion, and Blitz immediately moved his own chair a little farther away. Dexter sat between Cole and Gridlock, while Bullet Spear Man rested his weapon against the wall where he could reach it.
A server came to take their orders. Bulwark ordered enough food to make the young man check whether he had misheard.
"Yes," the tank said.
"All of those?"
"Yes."
Blitz leaned toward the server. "He’s feeding a building."
Bulwark ignored him.

The food arrived gradually. Dexter tasted the broth first. It was perfectly respectable—a little heavy on salt, and the meat could have been cooked longer at a lower temperature. He was examining the texture when Cole noticed his expression.
"What?"
"Nothing."
"You’re evaluating it."
Gridlock lifted his bowl. "He is evaluating it."
Blitz pointed his spoon at Dexter. "Next time, you cook."
Dexter looked at him. "You haven’t even tasted my food."
"We’ve seen the way you look at this one. Either you’re very good, or very bad."
"Both are possible," Gridlock said.

Dexter laughed and the conversation drifted back to the training—who should handle scouting, how much range they could maintain without losing mutual support, whether they needed to purchase shared equipment before accepting a gate mission.
"Whoooom!"
The sunlight disappeared.
He looked up, thinking at first that a cloud had crossed the sun.
But the change was too sudden. The bright courtyard outside darkened as though someone had lowered a curtain over it.
The fountain lights flickered on automatically, and a server stopped beside their table and looked toward the windows. Across the restaurant, conversations faltered.
"What happened to the sky?" someone asked.
Dexter slowly put down his spoon. Outside, darkness spread from one end of the facility to the other, flowing above the buildings in thick, overlapping waves.
Within seconds, the blue sky had vanished.

Chairs scraped across the floor as people stood. The courtyard filled with upturned faces. A broad dome of shadow had enclosed the entire Titan Training Center, its surface uneven and rippling with currents that moved against one another like black water.
The late-afternoon sun was gone, and so was the view of the city beyond the compound. Even the towers outside the facility walls had disappeared behind the darkness.
Cole rose. "Stay together."
Dexter was already on his feet. His first thought was his wives.

His second was the barrier. He took out his phone, but the message he sent did not deliver—the signal icon had disappeared. Around the restaurant, other people were checking their devices and reaching the same conclusion.
"What is this?"
"Some kind of facility test?"
"Nobody announced a test!"

A sharp alarm sounded from the central administration building, and the loudspeakers crackled. "Attention. All visitors and registered heroes—" The announcement cut off, replaced by a distorted hiss, and then silence.
Dexter’s expression hardened. "That’s not a test."

Near the main gate, several guards had already reached the shadowy boundary. One pressed a glowing access device against it—nothing happened. Another drew his weapon and struck. Dark ripples spread across the surface, and the guard was thrown backward. He hit the ground and rolled. Shouts erupted.

chapters.title: Chapter 307 | Attack II
paragraphs: Beyond the barrier, faint silhouettes appeared. People outside had noticed. A bright attack struck the dome from the opposite side, and for an instant the impact illuminated the black surface from within. The darkness swallowed it. The people outside remained outside, and the people inside remained trapped.
Gridlock stepped into the courtyard and extended a cautious thread of mana toward the barrier overhead. His face tightened immediately, and he withdrew it. "Don’t touch it carelessly."
Cole looked at him. "How strong?"
"I can’t tell. It isn’t behaving like the facility’s formations."
A man near the fountain suddenly launched himself into the air. "Move aside!" He carried a heavy blade glowing with concentrated mana, and several people shouted for him to stop. He struck the dome.
"KA-BOOOM!"
The sound rolled across the compound. For half a second, a pale crack seemed to spread through the shadow, and then the surface twisted.

The man’s attack disappeared into it, and a violent backlash hurled him down. He crashed through the branches of a tree and struck the courtyard hard enough to break the paving stones. People scattered, and a woman rushed toward him.
"He’s alive!" she shouted. "Get a healer!"
Dexter looked up. The apparent crack had already vanished. There was no opening, no weakness they could exploit—just darkness.

His fingers tightened around his phone. At home, there was a protection formation. There was a Transcendent guardian. Mira, Selene, and Lyra were safer there than they would have been beside him. He held on to that thought and put the phone away.

Suddenly, a long, tearing noise. Every head lifted upwards and they saw three thin lines had appeared beneath the shadow dome—one over the eastern training buildings, one above the central courtyard, and the third near the equipment halls to the west. The lines widened as space ripped apart.
Cole’s voice turned sharp. "Weapons!"
"ROOOOOAR!!!"
The first crack opened with a roar. A black shape fell from it, then another, then dozens. Dark wolves dropped onto rooftops, balconies, and the paved paths between the buildings.
Each was larger than an ordinary horse, with thick black fur and long limbs that bent low before springing forward.
Their eyes glowed a cold violet, and shadows clung to their jaws and streamed from their backs as they moved.
One landed on the roof of a reception booth, and the structure collapsed beneath it. A guard turned, and the wolf struck before he could finish drawing his weapon.
He disappeared beneath its weight, and blood splashed across the white wall behind him. The courtyard erupted.
"Monsters!"
"Fall back!"
"Protect the civilians!"
The second crack widened, and something shrieked inside it. Then the sky filled with wings. Wind-thorn Bats poured through in a thick, twisting swarm.
Their bodies were narrow and gray-green, their wings stretched across long jointed fingers, and thornlike growths lined their backs and tails.

They moved with unnatural speed, and the air bent around them. A cluster swept over the fountain, and their wings beat. Thin blades of compressed wind sliced downward. The fountain split, water bursting into the air.
A man standing beside it raised his arm too late, and he screamed and fell. Several others dropped behind the stone benches as more wind blades carved across the courtyard.
The third crack opened wider than the others. A huge green hand gripped its edge, and then a reptilian figure stepped through. Green Lizardmen.

The first landed on the roof of the equipment hall, crouched, then straightened. It stood well above the height of a man, with overlapping green scales covering its muscular body, a ridge of spines running from its head down its back, and a long tail that struck the roof behind it. It carried a crude black blade.
More followed—some wielded spears, others carried heavy clubs or hooked weapons made from dark metal and bone.
Unlike the wolves, they did not immediately scatter. They looked. Pointed. Roared commands to one another. Then they began moving toward the facility’s entrances and connecting passages.
Dexter saw one point at the administration building, and another group turned toward the main gate.
His stomach tightened as he realized that this was not a random spill of monsters, at the very least, some of them understood what they were attacking.
A wolf crashed through the restaurant’s front window. Glass exploded inward, and the server who had taken their order stood directly in its path.
Bulwark moved, his shoulder striking the creature before its jaws reached the young man.
"Bang!"
The wolf flew sideways through two empty tables, and Bulwark planted himself between it and the diners.
"Behind me!"

The restaurant changed in an instant. Tables overturned, people screamed, and a cook emerged from the kitchen holding a knife, saw the wolf rise from the wreckage, and froze. Cole thrust out his arm, and plasma flashed.
The wolf twisted—the attack burned across its shoulder and struck the floor behind it. It howled. The sound was wet and furious, nothing like a projected monster.
Dexter’s hand closed around the hilt of his Void Star Saber, and the weapon appeared in a flash. Its quiet hum reached him through the chaos as the wolf lunged again.
Bulwark caught it beneath the jaw, and its claws struck his chest. His shirt tore. This time, it eas real as blood spilled.
Dexter stepped beside him, and the saber moved once and the wolf’s head fell, its body crashing against the broken table.
For a heartbeat, the server stared at the corpse, and then Dexter caught his shoulder.
"Kitchen. Take everyone who can’t fight."
The young man stumbled.
"Move!"
He moved.

Outside, the facility had become a battlefield. Heroes were fighting in scattered groups—some had responded quickly, forming barriers around injured people and younger trainees, while others were still trying to understand where the attacks were coming from.
The monsters punished every moment of hesitation.
Dark wolves raced along the paths, dragging people away from broken formations.
Wind-thorn Bats swept across the open spaces, forcing everyone beneath roofs and overhangs.
The Green Lizardmen advanced through the confusion, smashing doors and cutting off escape routes.

An instructor near the fountain killed two wolves with a sweeping strike, but before he could recover, a rain of wind blades fell around him. He raised a shield, and a lizardman’s spear struck from the side.
He staggered, and three trainees rushed to help. One never reached him.
Dexter’s grip tightened.
Cole stepped beside him. "We need the staff and civilians out of the open."
"There’s no exit," Blitz said.
"Then we make somewhere to hold."
Gridlock looked back into the restaurant. "Kitchen should have a service corridor. Thick walls with fewer windows."
Dexter nodded. "Use that. Keep the injured behind it."
Bullet Spear Man was already scanning the courtyard. "Wolves coming right."

paragraphs: Finally!
The two kills he had needed had come almost as soon as the real outbreak began. Under different circumstances, he might have laughed out loud.
With 1000x he would have even more rewards but now wasn’t the time.
Another scream suddenly cut across the courtyard. Dexter dismissed the display.
He turned toward the restaurant. "We can’t stay here."
Cole glanced at the broken wall. "No."

The structure had lost too much of its protection. Even if Gridlock sealed every opening, they would be forced to spend more and more mana defending a building that the monsters could surround from all sides.

Beyond the courtyard stood one of the smaller training halls, its reinforced entrance open, and several instructors had already established a defensive position there, directing survivors inside while ranged fighters attacked from the upper windows. Dexter pointed.
"Move them there."
Gridlock followed his gaze. "About seventy meters."
"Can you cover the first half?"
"Yes."
"Then we clear the rest."
Cole nodded immediately. "Blitz, tell the instructors we’re bringing civilians. Bulwark, front. Spear, watch the roofs."
No one argued as the squad moved.
Far above the fighting, a man stood beneath the blackened sky.

He did not stand on a rooftop—there was nothing beneath his polished shoes as he simply floated in mid air, looking down at the Titan Training Center with an expression so empty that the destruction below seemed to bore him.
He wore a long gray coat over dark clothing, his hair combed back neatly, and at a distance he might have been mistaken for a government official inspecting a construction site.
Then he turned his head. His left eye was entirely white. There was no visible pupil, no iris—only a pale, lifeless surface that seemed to reflect none of the fires burning below.
Dravok, 9th on the continent’s most-wanted list.
There were villains whose names inspired fear because they commanded armies, others feared for the cities they had destroyed or the powerful heroes they had killed.
Dravok’s reputation was more personal. He only referee the weak. He peeled the flesh from his victims and wore it like clothing.
That single fact had carried his name farther than any official wanted notice. The white left eye was the detail survivors remembered him by.
Below him, wolves crossed the courtyard, Wind-thorn Bats wheeled between the buildings, and Green Lizardmen advanced through passages already littered with bodies.

Dravok watched without expression. His followers believed they understood the purpose of the attack—destroy the Titan Training Center, kill its heroes, make the Hero Association spend the next several weeks explaining how one of Stargate City’s most prominent training facilities had been turned into a slaughterhouse.

Those were their general orders. The second set of instructions had been more selective. Heroes with exceptional talents were to be captured alive. The young and the gifted, they could either turn them or extract their talent and gift it to their most talented members.
That objective had excited his subordinates more than the destruction.
But neither order was the real reason Dravok had come. His gaze shifted toward the blood spreading between the paving stones, and a thread of red mist rose from it—almost invisible.
The thread disappeared into the darkness overhead. Another followed from a dying wolf, then another from a villain crushed beneath an instructor’s attack.
Dravok’s white eye moved. All of them counted. Human, Monsters, heroes or villains.
Ten thousand souls and that was the minimum needed to awaken the Blood River Resonance.
The formation would gather them and the slaughter would feed it. And the people fighting most desperately to survive would help fill it with every enemy they killed. A faint smile touched his lips.
"BOOOOM!!!"
Suddenly, the highest tower in the training center shook as a figure rose from its roof.

The man was old, but there was nothing frail about him. His close-cropped hair was silver, his shoulders remained broad beneath a dark athletic shirt, and the muscles of his bare forearms were hard and lean. He wore ordinary training trousers and shoes that looked as though he had interrupted a workout to come outside. He looked down once—at the monsters, at the shattered buildings, at the bodies—and his expression darkened.
"Actually daring to attack this place?" His voice was calm, yet it carried across the entire compound. "Seems the Villain Association has started taking us for nothing."
Heroes below lifted their heads. "Director Rourke!" "The director’s here!"

For a moment, hope passed through the trapped defenders. Then Rourke turned toward the man floating beneath the shadow dome. He saw the gray coat, the motionless face, the entirely white left eye, and his expression changed.
"Dravok."

The name spread through the courtyard faster than the earlier cries of alarm. Dravok looked at him, and Rourke’s jaw tightened. "Shouldn’t you be hiding in the deepest pit of hell? Aren’t you afraid of the Hero Association hunting you to death?"

A cold chuckle escaped Dravok. "The Hero Association?" He tilted his head. "Hmph. They will be dealt with soon enough." Then he smiled. "You should worry about yourself. With the Nine Hell Chain Formation in place, forget about anyone coming in or going out."

Rourke glanced upward. For one brief instant, nine immense shapes became visible within the darkness—chains stretching across the dome in different directions, their links large enough to encircle entire buildings. Black symbols moved over their surfaces before the chains sank out of sight again. Rourke’s eyes narrowed, then he sneered.

"That’s fine by me." His aura rose, and the windows of the tower below him trembled. "I was worried you might flee." A pale light gathered around his fists. "Now I can kill one of the continent’s top nine wanted villains."

He moved. The air exploded behind him. Dravok raised one hand. Their first clash produced a boom that struck the buildings below like a physical blow, every window still intact rattling as clouds of dust erupted from cracked walls. Two Half-Step Transcendents collided above the Titan Training Center, Rourke’s fists burning with white light while Dravok’s hands moved through drifting shadows. Each strike shook the sky.
And beneath them, the killing continued.
Dexter heard the name—Dravok—and looked up only long enough to see the first collision. Then a wolf leaped toward the survivors, and his attention returned to the ground.
"Let’s keep on moving!"

chapters.title: Chapter 310 | Villian Invasion II
paragraphs: Bulwark walked at the front of the evacuation group, carrying one unconscious guard over his shoulder and using his free arm to knock aside anything that reached them.
Gridlock moved backward near the center, maintaining a slanted barrier over the wounded.

Wind blades struck it in rapid succession, each impact making the surface flash. Blitz appeared and disappeared along the route, dragging fallen people out of dangerous positions before the monsters could reach them. Cole and Bullet Spear Man covered the longer angles, and Dexter handled anything that got close.

A Dark Wolf lunged between two overturned tables, and his saber cut through it. Another came over the roof, and he caught the warning in the sudden change of air above him and stepped aside before its claws struck.
The beast landed badly, and Dexter finished it before it could turn.
Behind him, a trainee stumbled, and the girl beside him tried to catch his weight and nearly fell too. Dexter reached them in two strides.
"Arm over my shoulder."
The trainee obeyed, and they kept moving. A Green Lizardman stepped into the route ahead, dragging a heavy axe. Bulwark adjusted the unconscious guard on his shoulder. "Cole."
"I have it."
Plasma struck the lizardman’s weapon, and the axe flew sideways.

Bullet Spear Man’s thrust followed through the opening, and the creature fell. They reached the training hall with three wolves behind them and bats circling overhead. The instructors at the entrance opened a narrow path.
"Inside!"
The survivors hurried through, and a woman in a bloodstained training uniform began counting them as they passed. Dexter handed over the trainee he was supporting. "His leg is injured."
"I’ve got him."
"Two unconscious guards. Several cuts. One shoulder wound that won’t stop bleeding."
She nodded and shouted for medical supplies.
Only when the last civilian crossed the entrance did Gridlock release his barrier, his shoulders dropping. Cole looked at the instructor holding the door.
"Can you keep them safe here?"
"For now."
"What about the main gate?"
"Blocked. Emergency exits too."
"Anyone found a weak point?"
The instructor’s expression said enough. "We’ve been trying."

Dexter looked toward the western side of the compound, where the barrier curved down beyond the equipment halls. The monsters were thick there, but the route was shorter than the main entrance and less crowded with fleeing civilians. "We need to see it ourselves."
Cole nodded. "Agreed."

If there was a weak point, they needed to find it. If there was not, they needed to know before exhausting themselves trying to reach one. They left the survivors with the instructors and formed up again. This time, they had no injured people slowing them down. The squad cut through the courtyard.
The first street was full of Dark Wolves and the beasts moved in packs.
"Two behind the vehicle," he said.
Bullet Spear Man attacked without stopping, his spear thrusting through the vehicle’s shattered rear window. A wolf screamed. Cole’s plasma caught the second as it tried to escape, and they moved on.

Above them, the two Half-Step Transcendents collided again. A ring of pressure spread across the dome, and for a moment the shadow overhead thinned enough to reveal the outline of one enormous chain before darkness closed over it. Blitz looked up.
"If the director wins—"
"Watch the roofs," Cole said.
Blitz looked forward in time to avoid a descending wind blade. "Right."

They crossed a practice courtyard where several heroes were fighting around a damaged supply station. Dexter saw a young man pinned beneath a fallen beam, two wolves approaching him, and changed direction. Cole saw it.
"Thirty seconds. We hold here."

Dexter reached the beam and lifted. The trapped hero cried out as the pressure left his leg, and a woman rushed forward and dragged him clear. Dexter dropped the beam between them and the wolves, and the beasts hit the obstruction. His saber flashed twice.
"Get to the eastern training hall," he told the woman. "There are instructors holding it."
She nodded rapidly, and he was already returning to the squad. The squad pushed on.
The final stretch toward the barrier became a running fight. Wind-thorn Bats swept low across the road, and Gridlock raised a barrier at an angle, forcing them to change height.

Cole struck the climbing cluster, and burning bodies fell through the dark. Bulwark smashed a wolf into a concrete post. Bullet Spear Man kept the lizardmen from forming a line across the passage. Dexter moved wherever the pressure increased, his blade slashing through the beasts like the rotor of a blender.
By the time they reached the edge of the compound, their clothes were stained with blood and dust. Some of it belonged to the monsters and some did not.

The barrier stood less than ten paces away. Up close, it looked thicker than it had from the courtyard, shadows moving beneath its surface. Occasionally, something resembling a face seemed to press outward from within, then vanished before any one could focus on it.
Bulwark approached first, and Gridlock caught his arm.
"Be careful."
The tank placed his palm against the dark barrier and pushed hard but nothing happened.
"Bang!"
The ground beneath his feet crumbled and cracked, the radius increasing rapidly as he pushed even harder but the barrier did not move.
His arm began trembling, and then the shadows twisted.
"Boom!"
A force blasted back to him and Bulwark was thrown backward. Dexter caught his shoulder and helped him remain standing.
"That’s harder than i thought."
Bullet Spear Man stepped forward. "Let me try."
He gathered mana, and struck a single point.
"Ding!"
The impact rang like metal, and a ripple spread across the barrier.

For half a breath, it seemed to thin, then the force rebounded. Bullet Spear Man withdrew just in time as the returning strike tore a trench through the ground beside him. Cole’s expression became grim.
"It returns what you put into it."
"Not all of it," Gridlock said.
They looked at him, and he watched the dark surface. "Some disappears. Some comes back. I can’t see where the rest goes."
Dexter had said nothing. He was looking at his ring.
The Ring of Shared Burdens rested against his finger, unchanged in appearance.
He fed a thread of mana into it, and the familiar connection did not answer.
"What is it?"

"Not all of it," Gridlock said.
They looked at him, and he watched the dark surface.
"Some disappears.
Some comes back.
I can’t see where the rest goes."
Dexter had said nothing.
He was looking at his ring.
The Ring of Shared Burdens rested against his finger, unchanged in appearance.
He fed a thread of mana into it, and the familiar connection did not answer.
"What is it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 311 | Invasion III
paragraphs: Dexter did not immediately respond. During the first moments of the invasion, he had felt something strange—relief, a deep, sudden easing of the pain he carried for the girls.
He had been fighting, People had been screaming. He had assumed his body was reacting to the rush of energy. Now he understood that the pain had not eased, it was the connection that stopped.
The Ring of Shared Burdens had no distance limit. But distance was not the problem.

Whatever the Nine Hell Chain Formation had done, it had cut this place away so completely that even the ring could not reach across it. Dexter’s stomach tightened. They would be feeling those things again and be worried.
And he could not tell them why and could not even let them know he was alive.
"Dexter?" Cole repeated.
He lowered his hand. "It isn’t only a physical barrier."
Gridlock’s eyes narrowed. "You’re certain?"
Dexter nodded. "I have a connection to someone outside. It doesn’t depend on ordinary communication or distance."
"Gone?"
"Blocked."

Cole looked back toward the center of the facility, where Rourke’s fist struck through a mass of shadows and Dravok drifted away from the blow, his coat fluttering. Another tremendous boom rolled across the compound.
"Then we stop wasting strength on the boundary," Cole said.
Dexter nodded.
A scream rose from a nearby building. All six men turned. The sound cut off abruptly, and then a voice shouted, "Take that one alive!"
Dexter’s expression changed. That had not been a monster.
The voice came from a tournament hall. Its entrance had partially collapsed, leaving a narrow gap between a fallen sign and the broken doors.
Wolves prowled outside, and several Wind-thorn Bats clung to the exposed roof beams. Inside, someone was fighting. Dexter reached the entrance first and looked through the gap.
Four people in dark clothing stood in the center of the hall. Villains. He knew before he felt their auras.
The bodies near their feet and the restraints hanging from one man’s belt made the answer obvious.

At the far side of the hall, three young heroes had been forced against a damaged platform. One held a short sword, another stood behind a cracked stone shield, and the third used a metal staff to keep a circling wolf away from the injured.
Dexter’s gaze stopped on the swordsman. A familiar face. A familiar attempt at a smile, strained now by blood at the corner of his mouth. Simon.

The young man from the taxi, the one who had spoken cheerfully about the tournament while his sister criticized his chances of winning it. Dexter remembered the harmless grin, the easy handshake, the foolish warmth that had seemed so out of place among the suspicious people he usually encountered.
Now Simon’s sleeve was torn, blood running along his arm.
One of the villains raised a hooked chain. "Drop the sword."
Simon tightened his grip, and the villain smiled. "I didn’t say you would leave with your hands attached."
A wolf moved between the villain’s legs. It did not attack him and simply passed close enough for its fur to brush his trousers, then turned toward Simon.
Dexter’s eyes sharpened as another wolf crossed behind the remaining villains, ignored them, and the bats above shifted along a beam without striking at the four figures directly beneath them.
"They’re working together," Dexter said.
Cole crouched beside him. "I see it."

The villains carried similar black bands on their wrists, and the beasts avoided them as though the bands marked an invisible boundary. Whether it was a command, a scent, or some other technique, the result was clear—the monsters were only attacking one side.
Dexter examined the four villains properly, and his expression hardened. Peak Ultra Realm. All four of them. Cole felt it too.
"We need to—"
"You hold off the monsters," Dexter said.
The others turned toward him, and he kept his eyes on the hall. "Leave them to me."
Bullet Spear Man looked at the four figures, then at Dexter. During training, he would have questioned the order.
After fighting through the courtyard, he had seen enough to know Dexter had been holding back far more than any of them had realized. Still, four Peak Ultra opponents were something else entirely.
"Four?" he asked.
Dexter nodded. "Keep the beasts away from the people on the platform."
Cole watched him for one heartbeat, then gave the others their positions. There was no discussion about who should lead. Dexter had seen the opening. The squad trusted him to use it.

The chain flew toward Simon, and Dexter crossed the hall before it reached him. His saber struck the links, sparks bursting outward, and the broken end snapped into the floor. The villain holding it stared as Dexter landed between him and the platform.
"Pick someone else."
Simon’s eyes widened. "Dexter?"
"Stay back."

The four villains spread immediately. They were experienced—no one rushed him out of anger, no one wasted time asking who he was. The woman carrying a black staff moved left, a bald man with two curved blades moved right, the chain wielder withdrew his damaged weapon, and the largest of them, a broad-shouldered man with a heavy hammer, stayed directly in front.

Above them, the bats launched themselves from the beams. Cole’s plasma struck the first cluster, Gridlock sealed the approach to the platform, and Bulwark hit the wolves before they could gather. The squad’s battle began.
Dexter ignored it as his attention remained on the four villains.
The hammer came first, falling with enough force to crush the platform behind him.
Dexter stepped into the attack. "Asura Slaughter Demon Body." The change ran beneath his skin—his muscles tightened, and a darker pressure spread from him.

He met the hammer’s shaft with his left forearm and knocked the weapon off line. The floor broke beside his foot, and the broad-shouldered villain’s expression changed. Dexter’s saber moved toward his throat, and a chain wrapped around the blade.
At the same instant, black fire surged from the woman’s staff. Dexter twisted, and the flames struck the space he had occupied. The bald man appeared behind him, both blades aimed at his neck.
For one brief moment, all four attacks overlapped.

chapters.title: Chapter 312 | Kidnapped
paragraphs: "Whoosh!" "Ding!" "Bang!"
Dexter bent beneath the first curved blade, deflected the second, and kicked the bald man hard enough to drive him backward.
The chain wielder pulled, and Dexter let him—he moved with the force, closing the distance rather than resisting it.
The man’s eyes widened. Thunder rolled through the hall, and a silver light spread along Dexter’s blade as his Type-6 Blade awakened.
The chain instantly split apart.
The villain immediately pushed the gaurd against it and with a whoosh, the guard split apart instantly.
"Bang!"
Dexter’s saber slashed through his chest, and the man stumbled. Dexter immediately fleshed toward, slashing with his blade as he finished the man.
First one.
The hammer wielder roared, as his aura exploded like a shooting star.
The woman slammed the base of her staff into the floor, and black flames formed a ring around Dexter like a massive gate, cutting off his path.
The bald man blasted forward as he attacked through the fire as though he had done it a hundred times.
Dexter felt the heat close around him, and he chuckled. They had chosen fire of all the things.
The Abyssal Heavenly Flame stirred, and the surrounding black fire suddenly bent. For a fraction of a second, the woman lost control of her own technique. That was all Dexter needed.
"Void Godslayer Slash."
His saber fell, and a dark line opened through the flames. The hammer wielder raised his weapon, and the slash passed through it. The man’s roar stopped, and in that split second, he fell backward.
Second one.
The woman’s face changed slightly and she screamed. "Kill him!"
The second man was already moving, his body blurring. Six images spread around Dexter, each carrying the same attacks.
Dexter slowly shook his head. "Pathetic."
"Eightfold Lightning Severance."
Thunder burst through the hall, and eight brilliant cuts filled the space around him. The false images shattered, and the real villain tried to retreat but he was too late.
Third one.

The woman’s face change drastically and she immediately abandoned her staff technique and ran. Dexter followed with Flame Burst Step, heat bursting beneath his feet as he reached her before she reached the doorway.
She spun around raising the staff in both hands to block him but Dexter’s saber was at least Type 5. It sliced through her staff as though it was nothing, continuing as it slashed her into two.
The fight ended before the staff’s broken halves touched the floor.
Fourth!
Dexter stood for a moment. The immense amount of mana and strength he had used had not been small. Fighting four Peak Ultra opponents while keeping the battle away from the platform was stressfull.

There had been no room for a careless strike. Behind him, Cole’s final plasma shot struck a bat against the roof, and Bullet Spear Man killed the last wolf near the entrance. The hall fell into a tense, ringing quiet.
Simon stared at Dexter. So did the other two heroes.
Dexter shook the blood from his blade. "Anyone badly injured?"

The man with the stone shield introduced himself as Garran. He was broad-faced, with one eyebrow split by an old scar and a fresh wound running down his shoulder. The woman carrying the metal staff was Neris. One side of her sleeve had been burned away, and she kept testing the fingers of that hand as though checking whether they still belonged to her.
Simon lowered his sword slowly. "It really is you."
Dexter looked at him. "You still recognize me?"
Simon gave a breathless laugh. "You had the gold identification card. My sister talked about it foo."
"Is she here?"
"Not today."
Dexter nodded. That was one less person to look for. Simon glanced at the dead villains.
Then Garran spoke.
"They’ve been taking people."
Everyon’s expression changed, and Cole turned toward him. "Who?"
"The villains." Garran pointed toward the rear passage. "They came after the monsters. At first, we thought they were trapped too. Then they started cutting down anyone who resisted."
Neris tightened her hold on the staff. "But they didn’t kill everyone."
Simon’s expression darkened. "They checked identification cards and talent records."
Dexter thought of the black restraints. "How many?"
"We saw at least a dozen taken from this building," Neris said. "Most from the training wings. They knocked them unconscious and carried them away."
"Where?"
Garran shook his head. "We don’t know." He looked toward the barrier beyond the broken wall. "If they’re transporting captives somewhere, perhaps they’ve found a way through."

Dexter did not answer immediately. That possibility had occurred to him too, but it could mean several things—a hidden exit, an underground route, a storage space large enough for living captives, or something worse. He looked at the squad.
"Let’s follow."
Cole nodded his head, the decision did not make Dexter feel better. They had gone to the boundary looking for a way out. Now the people causing the massacre might lead them to one.
They searched the four dead villains quickly. But not one found a map. The black wristbands were more useful. Dexter lifted one with the tip of his saber, and a faint, unpleasant mana clung to it.
Nearby, a wounded wolf trapped beneath fallen debris stopped struggling toward them, its ears flattening as its gaze followed the band. Cole noticed.
"That’s how they’re moving through the monsters."
"Perhaps."

Dexter did not put it on. He passed it to Gridlock, who wrapped it in cloth and kept it separate from his skin. Until they knew how it worked, he had no intention of allowing an unknown object to bind itself to him.
Neris showed them the route the captors had taken. The passage behind the tournament hall led through a medical assessment wing.
Several doors had been forced open, records lay scattered across the floor, and there were bloodstains, broken restraints, and an abandoned shoe.
Dexter slowed beside one doorway. He could hear movement ahead but not monsters.
He immediately raised a hand, and the others stopped. A group of villains crossed the far end of the corridor.
Two carried an unconscious young man, another pushed a floating stretcher with three captives strapped to it, and the last walked backward, watching the route behind them.
Dexter drew the others into an empty assessment room as they waited, when footsteps faded, only then did he move again.

chapters.title: Chapter 313 | The Portal
paragraphs: They all followed at a distance as the fighting outside continued to shake the building, and once a tremendous impact overhead sent dust cascading from the ceiling.

Dravok and Director Rourke were still battling up above, causing shockwaves and either seemed able to end it quickly. Dexter listened for the captors, and then something else caught his attention—a strange absence.
The people ahead were still moving. He could hear their breathing, their heartbeats. Then, one after another, several heartbeats vanished all if a sudden.

Dexter’s eyes narrowed and he advanced another few steps, and the corridor opened onto a loading hall. He crouched behind an overturned transport cart and looked inside. A portal stood at the far end of the room.

It was narrower than the cracks in the sky—an upright oval of pale violet light, suspended between two temporary formation posts. Its center looked dark and deep, and occasionally the surface cleared enough to reveal another place.
Gray ground, tall, unfamiliar pillars and iron structures that might have been cages. Then the view clouded again.

A thin man sat on a low platform beside it, both his palms resting on a circular formation plate. Silver lines spread from his hands, connecting him to the portal’s edges. A spatial talent. Dexter understood almost immediately. The man was not maintaining an ordinary doorway through the wall. He was opening a passage into a different dimension.
A subordinate approached him. "How many more?"
The thin man did not open his eyes. "Until the order changes."
"The last batch is through."
"Then bring the next."
Two villains carried another unconscious hero toward the opening. The body passed through, and the heartbeat disappeared. Dexter’s jaw tightened. Beside him, Garran clenched his fist.
"We should go in after them."
Neris leaned forward. "If we wait, they’ll move them somewhere else."
Dexter shook his head immediately. "No."
Garran looked at him. "There are people in there."

"And we don’t know what’s waiting beside them." He kept his voice low. "We don’t know how many villains are on the other side. We don’t know whether we can return. We don’t even know whether that portal will stay open after we enter."

Garran looked back toward the violet surface. He hated the answer. Dexter hated giving it. But walking into an unknown dimension because they could not bear standing still would not save anyone. It would only give the villains more prisoners.
Cole studied the room. "How many?"
Dexter listened. Counted. Checked the upper walkway, then the side doors. "Twenty-five. Including the man holding the portal."
Blitz glanced around their group, nine.
Their original six, Simon, Garran, Neris. Twenty-five against nine.

Several of the villains carried Ultra Realm auras, most of the others were Superhuman experts, and the thin man at the formation plate was difficult to assess, his energy partially hidden inside the spatial fluctuations.
Bullet Spear Man watched the loading doors. "They’re bringing another group."
A wheeled platform entered the hall.
Six unconscious heroes lay across it, one so young that the sight made Cole’s expression change. Metal restraints circled their wrists, and a villain walking beside them checked a list.
"Two A-rank talents. The others were marked for further assessment."
The man beside the portal pointed. "Send them through."
Dexter’s eyes hardened. "We stop this batch."
"And the ones already inside?" Garran asked.
Dexter blinked his eyes but said nothing as he looked at the portal keeper. "We take him alive."

For the first time since entering the room, a clear possibility appeared. A person who could open the passage. A person who could identify where it led. A person the Hero Association might be able to force to cooperate. They could not rescue everyone yet, but they could stop more from disappearing. And they could keep a way to reach the rest.
They studied the room for another half-minute. Dexter would have preferred longer but they did not have longer. The platform carrying the captives was already halfway across the loading hall.

He pointed out the guards one by one. Five stood between the captives and the portal, two on the upper walkway, several near the loading entrance. The stronger fighters stayed close to the portal keeper. They had organized their defense around the assumption that the monsters outside would keep the heroes busy.
That gave Dexter one opening. Only one. After the first strike, everyone would know they were there.
"Gridlock, put a barrier around the captives as soon as we move."
The man nodded.
"Bulwark, get between the platform and the portal."
Another nod.
"Cole, upper walkway first. Spear, the loading entrance. Blitz, stop anyone reaching the controls."
Dexter looked at the three newcomers. "Neris, cover the platform’s left side. Garran, right. Simon, stay close enough to support either."
Simon tightened his grip on his sword. "Understood."
Dexter’s gaze returned to the five guards nearest the prisoners. "I’ll open it."
Cole caught his arm briefly. "After the first strike, call what you need."
Dexter met his eyes, then nodded. He would not fight as though he were alone. He had learned that lesson earlier.
The captives’ platform stopped. A villain reached for the first restraint and Dexter moved.
Flame Burst Step ignited beneath his feet, and he crossed the gap in a flash of heat. The nearest villain turned at the sound, and Dexter’s saber was already moving.

The first man fell before he could shout. The second raised a shield, and Blade Bloodline energy sharpened the edge of the Void Star Saber. The shield split, and Dexter passed him without stopping. The third guard reached for a communication talisman, and lightning struck his wrist. Dexter’s returning cut finished the attack.

The fourth tried to seize a captive and drag the unconscious body between them. Dexter’s expression turned cold. He stepped onto the edge of the platform, changed the angle of his blade, and struck before the man could lift the prisoner.

The fifth was faster as he abandoned the captives and leaped backward. Dexter followed. Thunder gathered along the saber, and a single brilliant cut crossed the space between them. The fleeing villain hit the floor.
Then the rest of the squad struck. Cole’s plasma engulfed the two villains on the upper walkway before they could attack the prisoners below.

Bullet Spear Man drove his weapon through the guard nearest the loading entrance. Blitz appeared behind another and brought him down before vanishing beneath a retaliatory slash. Bulwark slammed into the man beside the platform, and the impact carried both of them across the floor. Only Bulwark stood again.
Gridlock immediately raised a barrier around the captives.
A villain thrust a blade at his neck.
"Bang!"
Gridlock caught the attack against a small angled shield, redirected the man’s balance, and drove him into Bullet Spear Man’s returning weapon.

Then, one after another, several heartbeats vanished all if a sudden.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed and he advanced another few steps, and the corridor opened onto a loading hall.
He crouched behind an overturned transport cart and looked inside.
A portal stood at the far end of the room.
It was narrower than the cracks in the sky—an upright oval of pale violet light, suspended between two temporary formation posts.
Its center looked dark and deep, and occasionally the surface cleared enough to reveal another place.
Gray ground, tall, unfamiliar pillars and iron structures that might have been cages.
Then the view clouded again.
A thin man sat on a low platform beside it, both his palms resting on a circular formation plate.
Silver lines spread from his hands, connecting him to the portal’s edges.
A spatial talent.
Dexter understood almost immediately.
The man was not maintaining an ordinary doorway through the wall.
He was opening a passage into a different dimension.
A subordinate approached him.
"How many more?"
The thin man did not open his eyes.
"Until the order changes."
"The last batch is through."
"Then bring the next."
Two villains carried another unconscious hero toward the opening.
The body passed through, and the heartbeat disappeared.
Dexter’s jaw tightened.
Beside him, Garran clenched his fist.
"We should go in after them."
Neris leaned forward.
"If we wait, they’ll move them somewhere else."
Dexter shook his head immediately.
"No."
Garran looked at him.
"There are people in there."
"And we don’t know what’s waiting beside them." He kept his voice low.
"We don’t know how many villains are on the other side.
We don’t know whether we can return.
We don’t even know whether that portal will stay open after we enter."
Garran looked back toward the violet surface.
He hated the answer.
Dexter hated giving it.
But walking into an unknown dimension because they could not bear standing still would not save anyone.
It would only give the villains more prisoners.
Cole studied the room.
"How many?"
Dexter listened.
Counted.
Checked the upper walkway, then the side doors.
"Twenty-five.
Including the man holding the portal."
Blitz glanced around their group, nine.
Their original six, Simon, Garran, Neris.
Twenty-five against nine.

Several of the villains carried Ultra Realm auras, most of the others were Superhuman experts, and the thin man at the formation plate was difficult to assess, his energy partially hidden inside the spatial fluctuations.
Bullet Spear Man watched the loading doors.
"They’re bringing another group."
A wheeled platform entered the hall.
Six unconscious heroes lay across it, one so young that the sight made Cole’s expression change.
Metal restraints circled their wrists, and a villain walking beside them checked a list.
"Two A-rank talents.
The others were marked for further assessment."
The man beside the portal pointed.
"Send them through."
Dexter’s eyes hardened.
"We stop this batch."
"And the ones already inside?" Garran asked.
Dexter blinked his eyes but said nothing as he looked at the portal keeper.
"We take him alive."
For the first time since entering the room, a clear possibility appeared.
A person who could open the passage.
A person who could identify where it led.
A person the Hero Association might be able to force to cooperate.
They could not rescue everyone yet, but they could stop more from disappearing.
And they could keep a way to reach the rest.
They studied the room for another half-minute.
Dexter would have preferred longer but they did not have longer.
The platform carrying the captives was already halfway across the loading hall.
He pointed out the guards one by one.
Five stood between the captives and the portal, two on the upper walkway, several near the loading entrance.
The stronger fighters stayed close to the portal keeper.
They had organized their defense around the assumption that the monsters outside would keep the heroes busy.
That gave Dexter one opening.
Only one.
After the first strike, everyone would know they were there.
"Gridlock, put a barrier around the captives as soon as we move."
The man nodded.
"Bulwark, get between the platform and the portal."
Another nod.
"Cole, upper walkway first.
Spear, the loading entrance.
Blitz, stop anyone reaching the controls."
Dexter looked at the three newcomers.
"Neris, cover the platform’s left side.
Garran, right.
Simon, stay close enough to support either."
Simon tightened his grip on his sword.
"Understood."
Dexter’s gaze returned to the five guards nearest the prisoners.
"I’ll open it."
Cole caught his arm briefly.
"After the first strike, call what you need."
Dexter met his eyes, then nodded.
He would not fight as though he were alone.
He had learned that lesson earlier.
The captives’ platform stopped.
A villain reached for the first restraint and Dexter moved.
Flame Burst Step ignited beneath his feet, and he crossed the gap in a flash of heat.
The nearest villain turned at the sound, and Dexter’s saber was already moving.
The first man fell before he could shout.
The second raised a shield, and Blade Bloodline energy sharpened the edge of the Void Star Saber.
The shield split, and Dexter passed him without stopping.
The third guard reached for a communication talisman, and lightning struck his wrist.
Dexter’s returning cut finished the attack.
The fourth tried to seize a captive and drag the unconscious body between them.
Dexter’s expression turned cold.
He stepped onto the edge of the platform, changed the angle of his blade, and struck before the man could lift the prisoner.
The fifth was faster as he abandoned the captives and leaped backward.
Dexter followed.
Thunder gathered along the saber, and a single brilliant cut crossed the space between them.
The fleeing villain hit the floor.
Then the rest of the squad struck.
Cole’s plasma engulfed the two villains on the upper walkway before they could attack the prisoners below.
Bullet Spear Man drove his weapon through the guard nearest the loading entrance.
Blitz appeared behind another and brought him down before vanishing beneath a retaliatory slash.
Bulwark slammed into the man beside the platform, and the impact carried both of them across the floor.
Only Bulwark stood again.
Gridlock immediately raised a barrier around the captives.
A villain thrust a blade at his neck.
"Bang!"
Gridlock caught the attack against a small angled shield, redirected the man’s balance, and drove him into Bullet Spear Man’s returning weapon.

"There it is."
Dexter looked at him. "Scorching Fury."

Heat erupted from his body, the air distorting as the strengthening force of the bloodline skill surged through his muscles, increasing the power already carried by his tempered body. Dark flame curled around his shoulders. The villain’s smile vanished.

Dexter stepped forward. The curved sword came down, and he struck through it. Metal broke, and the man behind it fell. The spear wielder tried to retreat, and Dexter caught the shaft with his left hand, pulled, and the villain stumbled toward him. The Void Star Saber flashed.
Two.

Black chains wrapped around Dexter’s arm, and he did not stop. He dragged the chain wielder off balance and drove toward him with a burst of flame. The man tried to release the technique. Too late. Dexter’s saber entered his defense.
Three.

Four.

"Right side!"

Garran’s killer was moving toward the captives, and the villain who had struck Neris was following. Dexter changed direction. The first man barely had time to raise his weapon before Dexter struck him from the side. The second tried to flee behind the platform, and Blitz appeared in his path. The villain turned, and Dexter was there. The saber fell. The threat ended.
But the two heroes on the floor did not move. Dexter forced himself to look away. Later. If he stopped now, there would be more bodies beside them.

Cole’s opponent raised another mirrored shield, and Dexter’s lightning struck it from behind. The woman flinched, and Cole’s plasma hit the exposed opening. Gridlock’s swordsman lunged toward the prisoners, and Dexter caught him before he reached the barrier. Bulwark slammed his opponent against a support column. The blackened body resisted the first impact—not the second. Bullet Spear Man returned from the entrance with blood running down the shaft of his weapon. Simon killed his opponent near the platform. Blitz finished the final moving guard with a short strike beneath the ribs.

Suddenly, the room became quieter. Too quiet after the violence. Dexter turned toward the portal. The keeper had lifted both hands from the formation plate, and the violet oval began shrinking. The captives already taken into the other dimension were disappearing from view.
"Stop him!"

chapters.title: Chapter 315 | Betrayal
paragraphs: "Stop him!"
Dexter roared as he moved. The thin man leaped from the platform, a smaller spatial tear flickering beside his shoulder.

Dexter’s saber crossed the distance before the opening stabilized. The attack took the man’s legs out from under him, and he hit the floor with a scream. The small tear collapsed and the larger portal shuddered.

For a moment, the gray ground and distant cages became sharply visible. Someone moved beyond them—a figure turning toward the failing entrance. Then the violet surface folded inward. The passage closed. Silence rushed into the space it left behind.
Dexter stood over the wounded keeper. Alive. That mattered. The man was still alive.

Cole crossed the room slowly, blood running down his forearm. Blitz pressed a hand against his side. Gridlock leaned against the captives’ platform, breathing hard, while Bulwark checked the unconscious heroes for signs of life. Bullet Spear Man remained near the entrance, watching. Simon lowered his sword.
All six members of Dexter’s original squad were alive. Simon was alive. Dexter counted once, then again. Seven. They had entered with nine.

His gaze returned to the two bodies near the platform. Neris lay on her side, one hand still curled around her staff. Garran had fallen close enough that his fingers almost touched her shoulder. Dexter knelt beside them. He checked even though he already knew. No heartbeat. No breath.

Cole stopped beside him. For a while, neither spoke. They had known the two heroes for less than an hour. That did not make the space they left behind smaller. Neris had helped them understand where the captives were being taken. Garran had wanted to charge through the portal because he could not bear leaving strangers behind. Now neither would leave the training center under their own power.
Dexter lowered his head. A long breath escaped him. He had killed the villains. Stopped the transfer. Preserved six more captives. And two people who had followed his plan were dead.
Cole crouched beside him. "Dexter."
He looked up.
"We had to stop them."
Dexter knew. Knowing did not make it feel cleaner. He shook his head once, then stood. "Cover them."
Cole nodded. Dexter turned toward the portal keeper. There was still something useful he could do. He held on to that.

The thin villain dragged himself backward across the floor. There was nowhere to go. His eyes moved from Dexter’s saber to the dead guards scattered around the loading hall. Then he laughed. The sound was strained and ugly.
"You think you’ve won?"
Dexter stopped in front of him. "Where does the portal lead?"
The villain smiled. Blood marked his teeth. "You’ll never get them back."
Dexter looked toward the empty formation posts. The captives already transferred were beyond his reach. For now. He looked back at the man.
"You opened it. You can open it again."
The smile widened. "Perhaps."

Dexter crouched. The man’s jaw shifted—a small, deliberate movement. Dexter’s eyes sharpened, and he struck. His palm cracked across the villain’s face. Broken teeth struck the floor, and among them lay a tiny dark capsule that split when it hit the stone. A bitter smell rose from it. The villain’s laughter became a strangled sound.
Dexter seized his jaw before he could try again and checked that nothing remained hidden between the broken teeth. Then he released him. "You’re not choosing when this conversation ends."
The villain glared up at him, hatred replacing the smile. Dexter reached for the fallen formation plate.

A faint scrape reached his ears. Metal against cloth. His left hand moved, slapping aside the narrow blade shooting toward his ribs. The knife spun across the floor. The villain’s wrist bent beneath Dexter’s returning grip, and a cry escaped him.
"Pathetic struggle." Dexter’s voice was cold. He looked into the man’s eyes. "Don’t worry. When we hand you over to the Hero Association, you’ll confess everything."

Behind him, Cole was speaking to one of the captives who had begun to regain consciousness. Gridlock examined the restraints. Bulwark lifted a damaged section of the platform away from a trapped leg. Blitz stood near the doorway, listening for approaching monsters. Bullet Spear Man watched the corridor. Simon moved somewhere behind Dexter—familiar footsteps, a familiar heartbeat, another person who had survived the fight.
Dexter kept his attention on the prisoner. "Who ordered the abductions?"
The villain spat blood, and Dexter tightened his grip. "Who—"
A cold sensation touched the back of his neck and Dexter’s body reacted before his thoughts did.
The skin along his spine tightened, and something pressed against his back, sharp and impossibly fine.
"Ding!"
A needle, thin as a strand of hair had slipped through his torn clothing and struck his skin.
But it had not entered as his incredibly tempered body resisted it.
For one brief instant, the point remained caught against the dense layer of flesh beneath his shoulder. Dexter frowned and he began turning.
Simon was closely behind him at that moment.
The young man’s face held the same innocence expression he remembered from the taxi—the same apparently harmless concern in his face hand was already moving.
"Dexter—"

To anyone watching, it would have looked like a casual pat on the back. A grateful touch after a rescue. A tired companion reaching out to steady him. But Dexter saw the speed, the precise angle, the sudden concentration of force in Simon’s palm. Simon struck the exposed end of the hair-thin needle. The second impact drove it through.
Cold entered Dexter’s body. Not ordinary cold—it spread along his spine with terrifying speed, cutting across the movement of his mana. His hand stopped.
The portal keeper’s wrist slipped from his fingers. Dexter tried to step away, but his leg did not respond. He tried to speak, and nothing came out.
For the first time since the invasion began, his body ignored him completely.
Simon’s hand withdrew but his expression had not changed.
Dexter stared at him with wide eyes as the sounds of the room continued around them.
Cole asking a captive whether she could remember her name, the scrape of Gridlock moving a broken restraint, Blitz calling that the corridor was clear.
No one had seen. No one knew.

chapters.title: Chapter 316 | Poisoned
paragraphs: The sound of Dexter’s saber striking the floor cut through the hall.
Cole turned and saw Dexter’s knees buckle. For half a heartbeat, his mind went blank with confusing.

Dexter had just fought through a room full of villains, broken their strongest fighters, stopped the transfer of the captives, and captured the man responsible for opening the portal. Now he was falling.
"Dexter!"
Cole reached him a moment after Burke. The tank caught Dexter beneath the shoulders before his head struck the floor, lowering him carefully.
"Dexter." Burke shook him lightly. "Can you hear me?"
There was no response as his eyes were closed, his right hand lying open against the stone, inches from the saber he had been gripping so firmly moments earlier. Cole crouched beside him.
"What happened?"
Blitz appeared on Dexter’s other side. "He was standing a second ago."
"I saw that!"

"Don’t move!"
Dexter’s voice came out rough, but it came out.
The purple color began draining from his lips as warmth returned beneath his skin. He drew one breath, then another. The barrier crackled, and several needles blackened and curled inside it.

paragraphs: Cole stared at him. "Dexter?"
Dexter pushed himself upright, and Burke immediately reached to support him. He accepted the help for one moment, until his legs answered properly.
Then he stood as a thin line of dark vapor escaped between his lips, and the last trace of purple faded.
His face regained its normal color, though his eyes remained cold. Across the barrier, Simon had stopped smiling.
Dexter looked directly at him. "So you’re part of them."
Silence settled over the loading hall. Cole slowly rose, his gaze moving from the needles suspended in the flames to Simon, then back again.
Understanding arrived, and his expression changed.
"Simon?"
The young man looked at him, then at Dexter. A small chuckle escaped him. "Huh." He sounded more curious than alarmed. "You actually survived."
Dexter’s fingers curled, and the Void Star Saber rose from the floor into his hand. Simon watched it, then his smile returned.
"No wonder the others couldn’t kill you."

Cole’s plasma flared. Burke stepped forward, Blitz shifted toward Simon’s flank, and only Bullet Spear Man remained still, his weapon already angled toward the young man’s chest. Simon noticed all of them.
He did not appear particularly concerned.
Dexter lowered the flame barrier just enough to see the floor between them clearly. The ruined needles remained caught in a smaller pocket of fire near his hand.
"You attacked me."
Simon tilted his head. "You noticed."
Blitz’s expression twisted. "He saved your life."
Simon glanced at him. "Did he?"
"You were surrounded by four Peak Ultra villains!"
"And now they’re dead."
The answer made the room feel colder. Cole took a step forward.
"You fought beside us."
Simon’s eyes shifted toward the covered bodies near the platform, then back to Cole. "Yes."
There was no regret in his voice, no discomfort, nothing that suggested the deaths of Garran and Neris meant anything to him.

Dexter watched him closely. The easy grin from the taxi had not disappeared entirely, and that was what made it so unpleasant—the same face, the same voice, the same young man who had chatted about the weather and wished him luck in his spar.
Dexter’s jaw tightened.
"Who sent you?"
Simon shrugged. "Would an answer make you less angry?"
"Try."
For the first time, the young man’s smile thinned.

Dexter’s aura had begun to rise—not wildly, not in a burst of uncontrolled rage, but gathering around him with deliberate pressure, enough to make the loose dust near his boots lift from the floor. Simon’s gaze flicked toward the burning remains of the needles.

He had expected the first attack to end this. When it failed to penetrate properly, he had corrected it. When Dexter fell, he had believed the correction was enough. Now Dexter stood in front of him—alive, armed, and very angry.
"Who sent you?" Dexter repeated.
Simon spread his free hand. "You’re assuming the person who gives an order is the person behind it."
Cole’s eyes narrowed. "Stop talking in circles."
Simon ignored him, his attention remaining on Dexter. "Even if I knew the real name, why would I tell you? You might not recognize it anyway."
Dexter took one step, and Simon’s hand rose toward his collar. Bullet Spear Man moved immediately, his weapon shooting forward.
"Don’t!"

Simon caught the necklace beneath his shirt. A small pendant appeared between his fingers—gray metal with a clear stone at its center. Dexter felt a sharp disturbance in the surrounding space, and his expression changed.
He moved, Flame Burst Step driving him across the floor. At the same instant, Simon pulled the necklace downward. The chain snapped, and the clear stone shattered between his fingers.
For one fraction of a second, Simon’s body appeared to fold into a thin line of light.
"I suppose that’s enough for today."
Dexter’s saber cut through the space where his shoulder had been, but the blade struck nothing as Simon vanished.
Bullet Spear Man’s thrust passed through the same empty patch of air a heartbeat later, striking the wall behind him. Stone burst outward.
Dexter landed, his saber remaining extended. A broken length of chain fell to the floor. The pendant was gone. So was Simon.
Blitz reached the place where the young man had stood, looking toward the nearest doorway, then the upper walkway. "Where?"

Dexter did not answer. He was listening, searching for the familiar heartbeat. A moment earlier, it had been close enough for him to separate it from every other sound in the room. Now it was absent—like the heartbeats that had passed through the portal. Dexter extended his hearing as far as the chaos allowed. Monsters. Fighting and screams.
His grip tightened around the saber. Cole approached slowly.
"He teleported?"
"Some kind of spatial item."
"I thought the barrier stopped anyone leaving."
Dexter looked up toward the ceiling. "We don’t know that he left."
The distinction settled over them. Simon might have moved to another building, another section of the sealed facility, another space connected to this one.
His escape proved that he had prepared a way to disappear. It did not prove that the Nine Hell Chain Formation had opened for him.
Gridlock crouched beside the broken chain without touching it. "He was carrying that the whole time."
"Yes."
"And waiting."

Dexter lowered his saber. The anger did not leave him—it sharpened. Simon had watched him fight, watched the squad protect civilians, watched them follow the captors and plan the ambush. He had stood close while Dexter counted enemies and assigned positions. Then he had waited until the battle ended, until everyone was tired, until Dexter knelt beside the one prisoner they could not afford to lose, until a hand on his back would look harmless.
Cole looked toward the two covered bodies, and his expression became hard enough to hurt. "We brought him with us."
Dexter said nothing, because it was true. He had recognized Simon. He had remembered a friendly stranger. And he had allowed that memory to carry more weight than it deserved.
Blitz rubbed a hand over his face. "This is so messed up!"

chapters.title: Chapter 318 | The Counter Attack!
paragraphs: The ceiling shook before anyone heard the explosion. Dust sifted between the cracked panels, and then a deep, rolling boom passed through the loading hall, rattling the broken formation posts and sending a loose section of the upper walkway crashing to the floor.
Burke moved in front of the rescued captives, and Gridlock raised his hands. A translucent shield formed overhead just as pieces of concrete began falling.
Dexter looked up. Through a widening crack in the roof, he could see the black sky. Something golden flashed behind it, and Cole followed his gaze.
"The director?"

Dexter nodded slowly. The pressure descending from above was different now. Until that moment, the battle between Director Rourke and Dravok had been terrifying but distant—their attacks had shaken the facility, broken windows, and sent shock waves across the compound. Now the air itself seemed to be growing heavier. Dexter could feel it pressing against his skin, and the hair along his arms rose.
"Move them away from the outer wall," he said.
Cole did not ask why. "Everyone who can walk, help someone who can’t."

Blitz reached the first captive, and Bullet Spear Man took up a position beside the entrance with his weapon raised. Dexter remained beneath the crack in the roof for one more moment. Above the training center, the darkness was beginning to split around a growing golden light.

Director Rourke stood in the sky with blood running down his left forearm, his athletic shirt torn across one shoulder, and three dark wounds marking his side, each surrounded by traces of shadow that continued trying to burrow into his body. He pressed two fingers against the wounds, and golden light flared beneath his skin. The shadows burned away.

Across from him, Dravok flexed his right hand. Two fingers hung at unnatural angles. He caught them with his other hand and straightened them, and a faint crack sounded. His expression did not change.

Below them, the Titan Training Center burned. Smoke rose from the administration wing, a collapsed bridge connected two buildings that no longer had enough intact floors to support it, and monsters moved through the courtyards, their cries mingling with shouted commands and the screams of the injured. Rourke looked down—at a group of trainees huddled behind an instructor’s cracked shield, at a wolf dragging someone beneath an overturned vehicle, at the broken roof of a hall where he had taught students for more than twenty years. His jaw tightened.
Dravok watched him. "Distracted?"
Rourke lifted his eyes. "You’ve killed enough."
Dravok’s white left eye remained fixed on him. "Have I?"

The old man did not answer. He raised his right hand, and the golden light around his fingers narrowed into an edge. Dravok moved first, shadows bursting behind him and spreading into six dark ribbons that lashed across the sky from different directions. Rourke stepped through the first, and his hand cut down. The ribbon split. He turned his wrist and severed the second. The third wrapped around his ankle, and Dravok pulled.

Rourke’s body dropped sharply. At the same instant, a black spike appeared beneath him, rising toward his chest. He stamped downward, and golden force erupted from the sole of his shoe. The spike shattered. The ribbon around his ankle broke.

Rourke disappeared from his position, and Dravok’s right eye narrowed. A fist struck him across the face. The impact tore a path through the darkness behind his head, and he flew sideways. Before he could steady himself, Rourke appeared above him and brought both hands down. Dravok crossed his arms, and a black shield formed.

The shield buckled. Dravok was driven lower, toward the western practice grounds. He twisted in midair, released a wave of shadow, and forced Rourke to pull back before the darkness closed around his body.
For a moment, both men remained still. Their breathing was louder now. Neither could afford to treat the other casually.
Dravok touched the blood at the corner of his mouth, then smiled. "You’re stronger than your records suggest."
Rourke looked at him coldly. "You should have read them more carefully."

He spread his feet in the air. The golden light around him dimmed, then gathered inward. Dravok’s smile faded as the mana throughout the western half of the compound began moving. Streams of light rose from the air, from the stone, from the drifting smoke. They bent toward Rourke as though an invisible current had seized them. His shirt snapped against his body, and the wounds on his arm reopened beneath the strain. Blood ran across his fingers. He ignored it.

Dravok looked toward the old man’s hands, then upward. The darkness above Rourke began to churn. A golden point emerged, lengthened, widened. The light surrounding it became so bright that heroes below raised their arms to shield their eyes. An enormous sword formed above the director, its blade stretching across the sky for nearly a kilometer. Clouds of shadow rolled away from its edges, and golden symbols moved along its surface, each one burning with enough force to distort the air around it.
Rourke’s face reddened. The muscles in his neck stood out. Then he roared, his voice cracking under the force. "HEAVEN-SUNDERING SWORD!"
He thrust both hands forward. The sword moved.

Dexter felt the attack before he saw it. An immense pressure descended through the broken roof, and his knees bent slightly. Around him, several of the rescued captives cried out. Gridlock’s overhead barrier flickered.
"That isn’t aimed at us," Cole said, his voice tight.
"It doesn’t need to be," Dexter replied. He turned toward the inner wall. "There. Beneath the main support."

Burke lifted two injured captives at once, and Blitz carried another. The others moved quickly, gathering beneath the reinforced section of the hall while Gridlock shifted his shield above them. Dexter caught the portal keeper by the back of his clothing and dragged him away from the exposed floor. The villain looked upward, and for the first time since being captured, his face changed.

Outside, the giant golden sword crossed the sky. Its light washed over the entire facility, and for an instant, the shadows beneath the Nine Hell Chain Formation appeared thin and fragile. Dravok’s face turned pale. He thrust both palms forward.
"Open!"

Dravok moved first, shadows bursting behind him and spreading into six dark ribbons that lashed across the sky from different directions.
Rourke stepped through the first, and his hand cut down.
The ribbon split.
He turned his wrist and severed the second.
The third wrapped around his ankle, and Dravok pulled.
Rourke’s body dropped sharply.
At the same instant, a black spike appeared beneath him, rising toward his chest.
He stamped downward, and golden force erupted from the sole of his shoe.
The spike shattered.
The ribbon around his ankle broke.
Rourke disappeared from his position, and Dravok’s right eye narrowed.
A fist struck him across the face.
The impact tore a path through the darkness behind his head, and he flew sideways.
Before he could steady himself, Rourke appeared above him and brought both hands down.
Dravok crossed his arms, and a black shield formed.
The shield buckled.
Dravok was driven lower, toward the western practice grounds.
He twisted in midair, released a wave of shadow, and forced Rourke to pull back before the darkness closed around his body.

Their breathing was louder now.

"You’re stronger than your records suggest."

"You should have read them more carefully."
He spread his feet in the air.
The golden light around him dimmed, then gathered inward.
Dravok’s smile faded as the mana throughout the western half of the compound began moving.
Streams of light rose from the air, from the stone, from the drifting smoke.

His shirt snapped against his body, and the wounds on his arm reopened beneath the strain.
Blood ran across his fingers.

The darkness above Rourke began to churn.
A golden point emerged, lengthened, widened.
The light surrounding it became so bright that heroes below raised their arms to shield their eyes.
An enormous sword formed above the director, its blade stretching across the sky for nearly a kilometer.
Clouds of shadow rolled away from its edges, and golden symbols moved along its surface, each one burning with enough force to distort the air around it.
Rourke’s face reddened.
The muscles in his neck stood out.

"HEAVEN-SUNDERING SWORD!"
He thrust both hands forward.
The sword moved.
Dexter felt the attack before he saw it.
An immense pressure descended through the broken roof, and his knees bent slightly.
Around him, several of the rescued captives cried out.
Gridlock’s overhead barrier flickered.

"There.
