paragraphs: "Open!!!"
The other half of the sky churned.
Darkness gathered behind him in a vast, rotating mass. From within it, the outline of a gate emerged.
It was enormous, black pillars framing two doors covered in pale markings that seemed to writhe when looked at directly.
The doors trembled as something struck them from the other side. Once. Twice.
Then two huge skeletal hands forced their way through the narrowing gap. Their fingers curled around the edges of the doors, and bone scraped against black stone.
The gate opened and a freezing wind spilled out.
The hands released the doors and surged toward the approaching sword. Each was large enough to cover an entire building. The first hand struck the golden blade from the side.

The collision shook the sealed sky. A ring of white and black force spread outward, and below, several lightly reinforced maintenance structures burst apart. Their roofs vanished into clouds of debris. Heat swept through what remained, reducing the splintered walls to burning fragments. Trees snapped across the courtyards, and branches and stone benches spun through the air.

The skeletal hand held the sword for less than half a second. Cracks raced along its fingers, golden light shone through the joints, and then the entire hand shattered. Pale fragments scattered across the sky. The second hand closed around the blade, its fingers gripping tightly enough to slow the descending weapon. Rourke’s arms shook. Blood dripped from his nose. Dravok bared his teeth and pushed both palms farther forward. The giant hand tightened.

For one second, sword and bone remained locked together. The sound was unbearable—a deep grinding noise that seemed to come from inside the skull. Then the golden blade advanced another meter. The second hand broke. Its fingers tore apart one by one. The palm burst. The gate behind it convulsed and collapsed inward.

Dravok’s eyes widened. The sword had dimmed. Its edges were less distinct. But it was still coming. He crossed both arms before his chest, and shadows rushed around him. Layer after layer folded into a dark shield, each surface covered in twisting symbols. The sword struck. For a fraction of a second, Dravok disappeared inside a sphere of gold and black. Then the sphere shattered. His body shot downward.

The impact came like the end of the world. Dravok struck the western practice grounds, and the ground folded beneath him. A great depression tore outward from the point of impact, swallowing the broken training platforms and empty exercise courts around it. Earth rose in a vast ring. Concrete fractured. The shock wave spread across nearly half a kilometer, ripping through buildings already weakened by the invasion. Walls burst outward. Entire floors dropped. One long training hall leaned sideways before its damaged supports failed, bringing the structure down in a thunderous cloud of dust.

Rourke turned his hand as the force spread. The remaining golden light swept across the edge of the crater, forcing part of the blast upward and away from the nearest crowded shelter. It was not enough to stop the destruction, but it kept the collapse from reaching the entrance where dozens of survivors were gathered.

Inside the loading hall, the floor lurched. Gridlock shouted, and his barrier cracked. Burke planted himself beneath a falling support beam, and the weight struck his shoulders. His boots punched through the tiles.
"Move!"

Blitz seized the nearest captive and pulled her clear. Cole caught another before she fell. Dexter thrust his palm upward, and flame and mana met the collapsing debris, breaking smaller pieces apart before they could strike the people below.

The noise continued. It seemed to last far longer than it actually did. Then the worst of it passed. Dust filled the room, and somewhere nearby, water rushed from a broken pipe. Gridlock’s barrier dissolved. He bent forward, coughing. Burke shoved the support beam aside, and it hit the floor with a heavy crash.
For several breaths, nobody spoke. Then Cole began counting—one by one, making sure nobody had disappeared beneath the rubble.

Dexter stood still, listening. There were more screams outside, fewer monster cries near the western side, and far above them, the oppressive golden pressure had begun to fade. He looked through the broken roof. A vast cloud of dust rose beneath the shadow dome.
"Did he get him?" Blitz asked.
Dexter listened harder. Deep within the crater, a heartbeat continued. Slow. Heavy. Steady.
"No."

Dravok stood in the center of the crater. One knee had touched the ground. His left arm hung beside him, the sleeve torn almost entirely away. The dark shield was gone, and so was much of his coat. A long wound crossed his chest, and blood ran from it and fell onto the broken earth.
For a moment, he remained motionless. Then he slowly straightened. He lifted his right hand and wiped the blood from his lips.

Above him, Director Rourke descended through the thinning dust. The old man’s breathing was rough, and his right hand trembled slightly before he curled it into a fist. But his eyes were clear, and they remained fixed on Dravok.

"I’ve always wondered what it would feel like," Rourke said, "to kill one of the most notorious villains on the continent." Golden light gathered around his fingers again. "I think today I might finally find out."
Dravok looked up. His ordinary eye blazed with anger, and his white eye remained empty. "Dream on."

Rourke began descending, and Dravok did not retreat. Instead, his gaze shifted. He looked at the blood on the ground beside him, then farther away—beyond the crater, across the broken courtyards. Blood stained the entrances of the training halls. It covered shattered weapons and gathered beneath monster corpses and human bodies alike. Dark Wolf blood. The greenish blood of lizardmen. The darker stains beneath the bats scattered across the roofs. The blood of villains who had followed him here expecting wealth and victory. The blood of guards, instructors, trainees, restaurant workers who had simply arrived for another day’s work.
Dravok’s lips parted, and a laugh escaped him. Soft at first. Then louder. It rose through the dust, cold and ugly, until several fighters near the crater stopped despite themselves.
"HAHAHAHA..."
Rourke’s expression hardened. "What are you laughing at?"
Dravok bent slightly, one hand pressing against his wounded chest. For a moment, he seemed unable to stop. Then he lifted his head.
"Tell me something, Director."
Rourke did not answer.
"Why do you think I came here?"

chapters.title: Chapter 320 | Blood River Resonance!
paragraphs: The golden light around the old man’s hand sharpened.
Dravok continued. "Why do you think I risked my life entering a place where I knew you would be?"
"To die, apparently."
Dravok smiled. "Do you imagine I was bored? That I decided to seal myself inside a training center simply to exchange blows with you?"
Rourke’s eyes narrowed, and the smile widened.
"You’ve spent this entire battle trying to kill me."
"I still am."
"I know."
Dravok looked around again. "And while you were doing that, everyone else kept working."

Something cold moved through Rourke’s chest. He looked toward the nearest body—a dead wolf lying half-buried beneath a fallen wall. Its blood was moving. Not flowing downhill. Moving upward. A thin red thread rose from the broken stone and drifted into the air.
Rourke’s gaze snapped back toward Dravok. The villain brought his palms together.
The sound was small. A single clap. But the entire Nine Hell Chain Formation answered.

The hidden chains overhead became visible. All nine. They stretched across the dome like the ribs of an enormous cage. The symbols on their surfaces changed, black markings turning red. A low vibration spread through the facility. It passed through the buildings, through the ground, through the bodies of everyone still alive.
Dexter felt it in his teeth. The portal keeper beneath his hand suddenly began shaking, and Dexter looked down.
"What is he doing?"
The villain stared upward, his swollen mouth opening. No answer came.
Dexter tightened his grip. "What is it?"
"I don’t know."
The words came out thick and broken. For once, Dexter believed him. The man was terrified.

Outside, Dravok began to chant. The words were unfamiliar—harsh syllables struck together in a rhythm that made the surrounding shadows pulse. He spoke faster, his hands separating, his fingers moving through a sequence of signs. With each movement, another section of the formation lit up.
Rourke attacked. He did not wait for the incantation to finish. A narrow golden blade shot from his hand and struck toward Dravok’s throat.
One of the great chains moved—only its lower length. That was enough. It dropped between them, and the golden blade struck the black metal and exploded. The chain trembled. Dravok continued chanting.
Rourke’s expression changed. He shifted position and attacked again. Another chain descended. Then a third. They formed a moving enclosure around the crater, protecting the man at its center.
"You were using the formation to hold us here," Rourke said.
Dravok’s chant broke long enough for a smile. "Among other things."
Rourke looked across the compound. More blood was rising.

Dexter watched a thin stream slide out from beneath one of the dead villains. It moved across the floor, then lifted. A rescued woman cried out. The blood hanging from a broken edge of the platform rose in droplets, joining the stream. From every corner of the loading hall, dark red lines began drifting upward.
Gridlock raised a barrier across the nearest one. The blood struck it, spread over the surface, then thinned into mist and passed around the edges. Cole lifted his arm.
"Should I burn it?"
"Wait."

Dexter extended a small flame. The red stream recoiled from the heat. Part of it hissed and vanished, but something remained—a pale thread continuing upward after the blood around it had burned away. Dexter’s eyes narrowed. The thread writhed once, and for an instant, he thought he saw the outline of a face. Then it was gone.
His stomach tightened. "This isn’t only blood."

Blitz looked toward the covered bodies of Garran and Neris. His face changed. A faint red mist was rising from the cloth. He took a step toward them, and Dexter caught his arm. Blitz looked at him sharply.
Dexter had no reassuring answer. He could only see what was happening and understand that reaching into it blindly might give the formation another victim.

Above the ruined building, thousands of streams had begun gathering. They rose from every street and courtyard, from collapsed halls, from the mouths of the three monster gates. Blood lifted in long ribbons, crossing the air toward the crater.

The battles below faltered. Some heroes stopped attacking. Some villains did too. A masked man near the administration wing backed away from the corpse of his companion as something pale was drawn from it.
"What is this?" he shouted.
No one answered him. Dravok had told them to kill. He had told them whom to capture. He had never told them what happened to the dead.

The streams reached the crater. Dravok raised both hands. Blood curled around him in broad circles—human red mixed with darker monster blood, pale green fluid, and the strange colors of creatures that had poured through the gates. Under the formation’s pressure, the colors changed. All became red. Deep red.

The circling streams climbed. They gathered above Dravok’s head. At first, the mass had no shape. It twisted like a suspended storm. Then its sides began flattening. One surface. Another. Edges formed. Sharp corners emerged. The blood compressed. The pressure rolling from it grew heavier with every passing breath.
Rourke struck one of the enclosing chains with both fists. Golden light exploded. A link cracked. He forced it aside and drove toward Dravok.
The villain looked up. His chant reached its final line.
"Let the blood remember."
He closed both hands. The gathering mass stopped moving.

A cube hung above the crater. Ten meters high. Ten meters wide. Ten meters deep. Its surfaces were perfectly smooth, yet beneath them the blood continued to churn. Shapes moved inside it—too quickly to follow. A hand pressed against one face and vanished. Then the outline of a wolf’s head. Then something that looked horribly human.

Rourke stopped short. For the first time since recognizing Dravok, genuine alarm crossed his face. The cube pulsed, and a sound spread from it—low, vast, like a river rushing somewhere deep beneath the earth.
Dravok lowered his arms. Blood ran from his nose, but he was smiling.
"Thousands of beings," he said.
Rourke stared at the cube andDravok’s white eye reflected its red light.
"Heroes Villains Monsters. The formation was never particular and now, it’s finally complete."

The crimson barrier expanded violently, then dissolved.
What remained beneath it made the entire facility fall silent for one impossible moment.

paragraphs: "WAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!"
An astonishingly terrifying wail erupted from the cube like the screams of 10,000 demons.

In that split second, the sound rolled across the training center and struck every living creature inside it. Terror radiated through the entire facility and every one cowered in fear, m and absolute despair!
Heroes groaned as they dropped their weapons, covering their ears to block the horrifying shriek.
Villains trembled with dread as their hearts pounded. They also tried to close their ears but nothing helped.

The Dark Wolves bodies instantly flattened against the ground as they whined like little dogs while the wind-thorn Bats lost their rhythm in the air and crashed onto roofs, smashing tk the ground like meteors.
The Green Lizardmen fell to their knees, their claws digging into their own scales as though thag could stop the Wail
Inside the hall, everyone was also affected. Some screaming, groaning in pain and gritting their teeth as they tried their best to remain standing.
The rescued captives screamed as some of them fainted, another curled beneath the platform covering her head. Even the wounded portal keeper was rolling on the ground with his hands to his ears.
Far above the crater, Rourke raised a golden barrier before himself and his face was pale.
Dravok’s laughter stopped, and he trembled—despite everything he had done to bring this moment about, he too was affected.
Only Dexter remained standing without covering his ears.
At first, he thought the others were reacting to a pressure he had somehow failed to notice. He could also hear the wail but he wasn’t affected by the fear or terror.
Instead, a strange fighting rose from the depth of his head as his heartbeat grew heavier. The Asura Slaughter Demon Body stirred within him as a faint pressure moved through his muscles.
For one brief moment, he could feel a magnetic pulse attracting him from above. It was like a hunger deep within his bones, craving for food and theat food was the thing above!
Dexter’s expression changed.
’What is this?’
The connection was nothing like the Ring of Shared Burdens. If felt ancient and buried somewhere in his bloodline but now is awakened by the sound coming from the cube.
"Dexter..."
Cole’s voice dragged him back. The man had one hand pressed against his ear, blood seeping between his fingers. Dexter immediately moved, steadying Cole, then catching Gridlock before he collapsed.
The wail began to weaken.
Dexter looked up again and saw the cube suddenly started changing.
Its edges softened as the perfect corners folded inward as though pressed by invisible hands. Blood rolled across its surface and the mass stretched upward, then narrowed in the middle.
Two enormous legs separated from the lower half, descending toward the floor. The first foot struck, and the earth shook, the second followed, cracks spreading outward beneath it.
"Boom!"
A broad torso rose above the legs, chest was formed from densely compressed blood, but within seconds the surface darkened and hardened.
Layered bone armor appeared across it and it was blood red.
Shoulders formed, then armsa nd two immense hands opened slowly at the figure’s sides, each finger ending in a blunt, dark nail.
A neck rose between the armored shoulders and then, the head formed last. At first, it was featureless.
Then the blood drew back from a stern face with deep-set eyes and a mouth held in an expression of cold restraint.
A ridge of dark armor spread over its brow. Two swept-back projections rose from either side, resembling the broken crown of an ancient warlord.
The final streams of blood entered its body and abruptly, the wailing ceased.
A ten-meter-tall humanoid stood where the cube had been, motionless.
The silence around it was so deep that the crackle of distant fires became audible.
Dravok stood near one enormous foot, and for the first time since entering the facility, he looked small.
"Asuranti," he whispered.
The figure did not immediately respond. Its head remained lowered, its eyes closed. Across its chest, a pattern slowly brightened beneath the armor.
Dexter’s breath caught. He did not recognize the design completely, but he recognized the way its energy moved. His fingers tightened around the Void Star Saber.
At the crater, Asuranti inhaled. The remaining blood mist in the air rushed toward him. His chest expanded. Then his eyes opened. A dull crimson light burned within them.
Director Rourke raised his hand, golden mana gathering along his arm as multiple sword lights appeared behind him, but he did not attack.
Dravok lifted his bloodstained face. "Divine General, I have prepared your sacrifice."
Asuranti looked down at him. The pressure across the facility deepened. Dravok’s knees bent, and he forced himself upright.
"The enemies are—"
The giant turned his head. Slowly. Away from Rourke. Away from the monsters and the scattered villains.
Toward the damaged loading hall.
Toward Dexter.
The strange warmth in Dexter’s body surged. For one heartbeat, the distant crimson eyes seemed to meet his through every wall between them.
Dravok stopped speaking.
Dexter stood very still.
And the Divine General took his first step.
"BOOOOOOM!"

Asuranti’s foot struck the earth, and the crater trembled as his aura spread. It rolled across the Titan Training Center in a vast, invisible wave, passing through ruined buildings and shattered courtyards without slowing.
"THUD!"

A hero near the administration wing dropped to his knees, and another followed, then dozens more as weapons struck the ground. Below the Ultra Realm, those who had managed to remain standing were forced down almost instantly, and some tried to resist only for their legs to buckle beneath them.

The monsters fared no better. Dark Wolves pressed their bellies against the earth, and Wind-thorn Bats clung desperately to broken walls, their wings trembling. Inside the loading hall, Burke planted both hands against the platform holding the rescued captives, and his arms shook.
"Damn it..."

One knee struck the floor as, beside him, Blitz caught a support column and held on. Gridlock bent forward, his face pale, and Bullet Spear Man drove his weapon into the ground and leaned against it, gritting his teeth as the pressure forced his shoulders lower. Cole’s breathing became uneven.
"T-that’s..."
His voice caught.
"A Transcendent-level expert."
